decisions.executionNote: Approach the nearer two white supports with open grippers, gradually tilting both wrists while retaining elbow-up continuity. Layout differs from the reference.
Align wrists with the two nearer blocks' yaw and lower toward their sides. Estimated fingertip offset and height will be checked in wrist views before closing.
Correct small lateral offsets in the wrist views, close on both supports, then lift vertically to verify retention visually.
Both blocks appear retained. Carry them above the two lower-support sites, straightening their yaw together while keeping the grippers closed.
Lower both retained supports onto the table at symmetric sites, open only after settling, then begin a short vertical withdrawal.
Withdraw from the released supports and move outward above the long board's ends, rotating the wrists for a coordinated two-ended grasp.
Replan from the accepted prefix using smaller outward and wrist-rotation increments to respect the joint-continuity guard.
Finish the outward clearance and opposing board-grasp orientations with smaller rotations; both released supports appear upright.
Bring both grippers down and inward to the long board's ends, then close simultaneously without changing the board's orientation.
Keep both grips closed and lift the long board evenly above the support height; verify retention and levelness from the next views.
The board is visibly retained and level. Translate it over the symmetric lower supports, then approach their tops slowly while keeping both grips closed.
Seat the lower board on both upright supports, pause, release both ends, and withdraw outward/upward without disturbing the centered layer.
The lower board appears stable after release. Reorient the open wrists above it toward the two remaining white blocks, keeping vertical clearance.
Align above the remaining blocks with their visible yaw, descending only to a clearance height before checking the wrist views.
Refine left alignment and descend. Correct the right block's yaw from its wrist view, shifting the wrist around the block rather than pushing it.
Avoid further pushing against the lower board. Test a shallow left-block grasp and lift; shift the right gripper outboard to center on its block before lowering cautiously.
The left block was not retained and the right approach contacts the board. Open and lift, changing to a steeper overhead approach to avoid the completed layer.
Descend slowly with the steeper wrists and open jaws, refining alignment from the head view while keeping the right wrist slightly outboard of the lower board.
Lower the overhead fingertips to the upper sides of the blocks, close, and make a short vertical retention test. The right block remains close to the board edge.
The shallow closure did not securely retain the blocks. Reopen, clear upward, and shift toward their far sides to center the overhead grasp rather than contact their near edges.
Refine overhead centering from the wrist images, aligning the left wrist with the block's changed yaw. Descend in small increments with both jaws open.
Center and test the left overhead grasp. Clear the right wrist away from the board and turn to an outboard approach so its jaws need not descend against the board.
Replan with smaller vertical increments. The left jaws appear to have closed above the block, so reopen and lower further; continue a shallower outboard approach on the right.
Test the deeper left grasp with a vertical lift. Back the right gripper clear of the board and align it with the block's exposed outer end before approaching again.
The left block is visibly lifted. Carry it upright toward the middle-layer support site while straightening yaw; test a right-block grasp at its exposed outer end.
Seat the retained left block on the lower board and release. The right block is not retained; reopen and correct its lateral alignment from the wrist image before another approach.
The left middle support is upright on the board. Withdraw that arm while lowering the now-centered right jaws farther, then close and test a vertical lift.
The right block appears between the jaws. Lift it clear of the lower board to verify retention while moving the empty left wrist toward the middle board approach.
Carry the retained right support over the right middle-layer site without changing its level orientation. Position the empty left gripper above the near board's left end.
Center the right support relative to the left one, lower onto the board, release, and withdraw slightly. Finish aligning the left gripper at the middle board's end.
Both middle supports now appear upright. Hold the near board's left end without lifting, and bring the right gripper clear of the tower toward its opposite end.
Lower the right gripper to the middle board's end, close both grips, and start a small synchronized lift to check retention.
Lift the middle board evenly with both grippers closed, clearing the upright middle supports before translating over the tower.
The middle board is visibly retained and level. Carry it over the two upright middle supports, centering on their observed midpoint.
Lower the level middle board onto both upright supports, allow it to settle, release both ends, and begin a small outward withdrawal.
The middle board remains centered after release. Withdraw both open grippers and approach the small wooden board on the left and the green top piece on the right.
Align the left gripper across the small board's narrow sides and lower both wrists toward the two top pieces, keeping the jaws open for visual alignment.
Correct each top piece's visible yaw and lateral alignment, close around their sides, and lift briefly to check that both are retained.
Both top pieces appear retained. Raise them clear of the tower, rotate the small board toward the layer's long axis, and hold the green piece off to the right.
Carry the small board above the middle layer and continue its horizontal yaw alignment. Keep the green piece raised and separate on the right.
Finish centering and yaw alignment of the retained small board, descending slowly toward the middle board while the right arm holds the green piece aside.
Make a small centering correction, seat the small board on the middle layer, release it, and withdraw the left gripper. Keep the green top piece stationary and retained.
The released small board's orientation is uncertain in the current view. Clear the left fingers farther away and allow settling before placing the green piece.
The middle board has slid off while the supports remain upright. Return the green piece safely to the table to free both arms, and approach the fallen middle board for recovery.
Set down and release the green piece. Reposition the left wrist farther forward and outboard so its jaws can reach the fallen board without pressing on the lower layer.
Use a narrower opening to approach the fallen board's left end without reaching into the lower layer, then test retention. Bring the free right wrist above the opposite end.
Recenter both jaws on the fallen board's ends and close together. Make a short synchronized lift and forward withdrawal to test a level recovery grasp.
The recovery grasp contacted the lower layer and skewed the fallen board. Release both jaws immediately and withdraw forward/upward so the pieces can settle before a clearer approach.
The long board is now tipped and the layers need recovery. Move the closed left fingers above its rear side for a cautious flattening maneuver, keeping the right arm clear.
Use small forward/downward contact increments at the tipped board's upper edge, then lift clear to inspect whether it has settled flat. The other arm remains stationary.
The previous motion did not visibly flatten the board. Lower the closed fingertips closer to its rear upper edge in small increments, then nudge toward the front while avoiding the white supports.
The tipped board is not responding to the light nudge. Reposition both open grippers at its outer ends for a controlled recovery grasp instead of further pushing near the supports.
Center the right jaws on the tipped board to match the left, close at both outer ends, and test a short even lift before attempting to level it.
The board appears pinched at both ends. Lift it clear of the loose supports, then begin a small coordinated roll toward horizontal, compensating wrist position around the grasp line.
Continue rolling the retained long board toward horizontal in small synchronized increments, keeping it elevated above the loose pieces.
The visible face suggests the roll was toward the underside. Reverse it cautiously while translating the elevated board toward the front pair of supports, keeping both grips closed.
The left end may have slipped. Recenter and reclose that jaw while the right holds, then resume a smaller counter-roll toward the board's upright horizontal orientation.
Only the right end is retained. Clear the empty left arm and cautiously counter-roll the board with the right wrist, maintaining its grasp-point height before reassessing its levelness.
Move the long board forward away from the other pieces and lower it for a table reset. Release only after the descent so it can settle flat before a fresh level grasp.
The long board has settled broad-face up. Restore both wrists to level board-grasp orientations and align over its ends for a fresh two-handed lift.
Lower both jaws to the now-flat long board, close symmetrically, and test a short level lift before returning it to the front pair of upright supports.
The long board remains broad-face up between the jaws. Lift clear and translate it over the front support pair, using its observed center rather than assuming a centered grasp.
The left grip has slipped but the right still retains the level board over both supports. Seat it with a short vertical descent, release, and clear both ends without rolling it.
The board settled in front of the support tops rather than on them. Reapproach both ends at its current height and yaw for a corrected placement farther back.
Close on the board's current ends and lift clear with small leveling corrections. Confirm the board is retained before making the backward placement correction.
Only the right end is retained. Clear the empty left gripper and carry the level board farther back over the front supports, stopping above them to check alignment before release.
The board now visually spans both front supports. Lower vertically to their tops, pause, and open the right gripper without lateral motion so the layer can settle.
Clear the released board without touching its edges. Begin a high, steep approach toward the rear-left loose support while keeping the right arm out of the tower workspace.
Continue the left overhead approach to the rear-left block with the jaws open, leaving clearance above the board and keeping the right arm stationary.
Replan after the continuity rejection: use smaller increments, stop the forward reach, and finish the left overhead orientation while lowering toward a visual alignment check.
The vertical left approach reached its IK margin. Tilt slightly shallower and retreat the wrist while centering the fingertips; begin an outboard approach to the rear-right block with the other arm.
The last action moved neither arm. Halve the left retreat and tilt increments to stay within the joint-continuity limit while the right approaches its block.
Refine the left block centering, close at a deeper side-grasp height, and test a short lift. Align the right gripper at the rear-right block's outer side without crossing the arms.
